candidates.text: to be clear, these weren't people deciding that Bitcoin was dead. This was forced selling, positions closed by an exchange, and not by their owners.

Bitcoin's short -term holders sold $11.3 billion worth of Bitcoin right at the bottom before, of course, it immediately bounced 10%, and now is pumping up to around $64,000. Largely on the news, the Jensen Huang is back as CEO of NVIDIA, which just hit the tape.

Bitcoin's keenest buyers that afternoon were actually people who had bet against it. So, capitulation tells you who has finished selling. But it doesn't tell you much about who is going to buy. And if nobody chose to buy the bounce, where has the buying money actually gone?

By the way, $11.3 billion of short -term holders in Bitcoin, that's retail holders trading, capitulated on those lows, which is a historically high number and aligns with all the other bottoms. sellers finally have enough pain, short -term holders, and they sell right into the low, right into the smart money, right?

Analysts say that the amount of money sitting at a loss in Bitcoin has never been higher. Bitcoin's last bear market bottomed on November 21st of 2022. The price was about 15,500. And this low came four years later almost to the day.

to be clear, these weren't people deciding that Bitcoin was dead. This was forced selling, positions closed by an exchange, and not by their owners. And it wasn't as historic as it first looked either. By the time the counting stopped, the total was about $2.7 billion.
